newsitem.title: FRANCE: France snipes at Washington over Mideast summit.
newsitem.headline: France snipes at Washington over Mideast summit.

text.p: France sniped at Washington on Friday for scant results of a Middle East summit and said Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak should play a major role in trying to revive the Israeli-Palestinian peace process.

"A meeting prepared in other conditions would have allowed concrete results," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said of the emergency summit at the White House that ended with no breakthroughs apart from a deal to keep talking.

"The positions are still very far apart," he told reporters hours before a visit by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to brief French President Jacques Chirac on the results of the two-day summit he had with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
France had previously faulted U.S. President Bill Clinton for failing to invite European leaders to the White House meeting on Tuesday and Wednesday.

"(Egyptian) President Hosni Mubarak, whose insight and authority are well known, will certainly have a major role to play in the talks to follow," he added. Fifty-eight Arabs and 15 Jews have died in fighting since last week.
Mubarak, who declined to attend the Washington summit aimed at ending the violence, said on Friday that Netanyahu's policies were setting the Arab world "on fire".

Rummelhardt also said "France hails the efforts of the parties concerned to revive the peace process." Israelis and Palestinians have agreed to hold new talks at the Erez crossing between Gaza and Israel from Sunday.
Rummelhardt said it was essential for the Erez talks quickly to lead to results in implementing the existing Middle East peace accords.
